o: Each equation Ai/Bi = vi constrains ratios between variables; we must detect any inconsistency, treating doubles equal within 1e-5. This is the classic weighted union-find / graph-ratio-propagation problem: within a connected component, fixing one variable determines all others multiplicatively, and a contradiction appears when a new equation conflicts with previously derived ratios. Only ~100 equations, so either DSU or BFS labeling is cheap.
k: Weighted DSU stores, for each node, its ratio to its component root; union merges roots with the appropriate multiplicative correction.
When an equation links two nodes already in the same component, compare the derived ratio to the stated one within 1e-5.
Equivalent alternative: BFS/DFS assigns each variable an absolute value (seed = 1) and every edge is re-verified.

a.n: Approach 1: Weighted Union-Find with path compression
a.i: find(x) returns (root, x/root), compressing paths by multiplying ratios. To union a/b = v with roots ra, rb and ratios xa, xb: set parent[ra] = rb and rel[ra] = v * xb / xa so that a's ratio to the new root stays consistent. If ra == rb already, the equation is redundant and must satisfy |xa/xb - v| <= 1e-5, else contradiction.
s: Map variables to DSU entries lazily; rel[x] = ratio of x to its parent.
find recursively: attach x to its grandparent and multiply rel[x] by the parent's ratio.
For each equation, find both sides; if roots differ, link roots with rel[ra] = v * xb / xa.
If roots match, check |xa / xb - v| <= 1e-5; otherwise return true (contradiction).
a.t: O(E alpha(V)) — near-linear union-find over at most 200 variables.

a.n: Approach 2: Graph BFS with absolute values
a.i: Model variables as nodes and equations as weighted directed edges (a -> b with weight v meaning a = v*b). BFS each component assigning each node an absolute value (seed node = 1); afterwards, re-check every equation against assigned values. Any mismatch beyond 1e-5 signals a contradiction. This avoids amortized-DSU reasoning and is easy to debug.
s: For each unassigned node, BFS setting val[next] = val[cur] * weight.
After labeling, verify every equation: |val[a]/val[b] - v| <= 1e-5.
Return true on any violation, else false.
a.t: O(V + E) — each node and edge processed a constant number of times.
a.sp: O(V + E) — adjacency list and value map.

w: Weighted DSU is the canonical answer; BFS labeling is a great sanity-check alternative. Pitfalls: epsilon comparison direction (use > 1e-5 for contradiction), division-by-zero is impossible since values > 0, and self-equations a/a = v which must equal 1. Follow-up: report which equation first contradicts, or handle values that can be zero/negative.
